therapeuticClass: Oncology — Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor — PD-1 Inhibitor
indication: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); melanoma; head and neck squamous cell carcinoma; triple-negative breast cancer; colorectal cancer (MSI-H/dMMR); endometrial carcinoma; cervical cancer; TMB-high solid tumors; Hodgkin lymphoma; bladder cancer; esophageal/GEJ adenocarcinoma; renal cell carcinoma; and other FDA-approved tumor types
quantityLimit: Per treatment cycle as documented in oncology treatment plan; quantity per fill tied to cycle length (typically 21-day or 42-day cycles)
quantityLimitReason: Oncology dosing is cycle-based. Quantity limit exception required if cycle deviates from standard 200 mg every 3 weeks or 400 mg every 6 weeks.
preferredSpecialtyPharmacy: HealthBridge Specialty Pharmacy (preferred); may also be dispensed through oncology center buy-and-bill under J-code J2357
formularyNotes: Pembrolizumab (Keytruda) is a PD-1 immune checkpoint inhibitor. Covered for all FDA-approved oncology indications per NCCN Category 1 or Category 2A recommendations. PA requires histologic confirmation, staging documentation, and — for NSCLC — PDL1 IHC testing. MSI/MMR testing required for CRC and endometrial indications. No step therapy required for oncology. Buy-and-bill J-code J2357 (pembrolizumab, 1 mg) under medical benefit is an alternative dispensing pathway.
clinicalAlerts: Immune-mediated adverse reactions (pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies, nephritis) — monitor closely
Withhold or permanently discontinue based on severity of immune-related reactions
Infusion-related reactions: premedication protocols may be required
Not recommended in patients with active autoimmune disease on systemic immunosuppression
Refrigerate 2°C–8°C; do not freeze; do not shake
